entrypoints.summary: The TCP listener on 0.0.0.0:10021 accepts remote connections; authenticate reads the selected username and then password bytes from the connection.
The compose configuration publishes TCP port 10021.

affected_components.role: Password validation conditionally establishes admin state; file service bypasses protected-name filtering for that state.
Runs the server as user ctf and gives group ctf read access to files under secret and public.

causal_paths.kind: admin state to protected file read

code_slices.fixed: No fixed code or patch is included.
code_slices.surrounding_context: pynetfs_main calls serve only after authentication; Dockerfile runs the server as ctf and sets secret files to mode 440 with group ctf.
code_slices.vulnerable: authenticate loops over the secret password, receives one byte at a time, and returns immediately on the first mismatch; serve skips its protected-name test for is_admin and calls open(filepath, 'rb').

observability.channel: TCP response timing or connection completion during authentication; on successful authentication, returned file bytes.
negative_controls: Incorrect password response or authentication return for a mismatching candidate.
Permission denied response when a non-admin request path contains a protected name.
observability.positive_marker: Logged in response followed by bytes returned for the requested file.

preconditions: The remote service is reachable on published TCP port 10021.
Practical prefix timing/connection-completion distinguishability is assumed but not demonstrated by an execution artifact.
The target protected file is readable by the ctf service account after admin authentication.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: admin username followed by a candidate byte sequence and newline
trigger_steps.summary: Select admin and submit password candidates whose correct-prefix length is varied to obtain authentication-path observations.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: newline-terminated path such as a file beneath secret
trigger_steps.summary: After obtaining valid admin authentication, submit a protected filepath at the File prompt.

relation_candidates.rationale: The TCP authentication interface accepts attacker-selected password bytes, and its bytewise early-return path has secret-prefix-dependent work.
Prefix-dependent observations may be used to infer the admin password; accepted admin authentication sets the admin identity.
The protected-name filter is applied only when is_admin is false; the service subsequently opens the supplied filepath and sends file bytes.
The runtime places secret files in the service working directory with group read permission for the ctf service account, and a flag target is present in the supplied bundle.

A complete bounded comparison without prefix-dependent early exit removes the particular per-byte early-return timing path shown by the source; this is an inferred remediation because no patch is present.

impact.affected_asset: The secret directory content, including the packaged flag target
impact.attacker_capability: Use prefix-dependent authentication observations to attempt admin-credential recovery, authenticate as admin, and request a protected filepath
impact.security_effect: Potential disclosure of protected files available to the ctf service account after inferred admin authentication

causal_trace.summary: A remote TCP peer can select the admin username and provide password bytes to the authentication routine.

Admin-password checking does not make the amount of password-processing work independent of the matched secret prefix: it reads and compares one byte per loop iteration and returns on the first unequal byte or closed connection.

The interactive bytewise comparison performs a prefix-dependent number of blocking recv(1) calls before emitting an incorrect-password response or returning, exposing a timing/connection-completion observation whose duration depends on the comparison path.

If the admin credential is recovered and accepted, is_admin disables the protected-name check; serve then opens the client-supplied path and returns up to MAX_SIZE bytes. The packaged runtime makes secret files group-readable to the ctf service user, and the bundle contains a flag target in that directory.

failure.operation: Early-returning bytewise password comparison coupled to blocking single-byte receives

primary_invariant.statement: Admin authentication must not expose a secret-prefix-dependent password-processing path to a remote peer.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The routine compares attacker-provided bytes to the secret one at a time and exits immediately on the first mismatch, rather than completing a bounded credential check with comparison work independent of the matching prefix.

quality.review_notes: The source and runtime directly establish the early-exit bytewise authentication path, admin-gated pathname check, file-read behavior, and service-file permissions. No organizer-origin artifact, exploit transcript, timing measurements, successful credential recovery, test execution, or remediation patch is supplied. Network jitter and practical reliability of prefix timing recovery are therefore unverified.

remediation.invariant_restored: Collect a bounded complete credential and compare it without secret-prefix-dependent early exit or interactive per-byte receive timing; retain the admin authorization check before protected-file access.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: A remote client can connect to the published TCP service, choose admin as the username, and submit candidate password bytes.
data_structure_invariants: LOGIN_USERS maps admin to bytes read from secret/password.txt.
is_admin requires both authenticated state and user equal to admin.
Non-admin file requests whose paths contain server.py or secret are denied.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: A successful file request returns at most 0x1000 bytes per read.
numeric_domains.name: MAX_SIZE

state_context.state_machine: Unauthenticated connection -> username accepted -> bytewise password comparison -> authenticated/admin state only after complete exact password plus newline -> file-serving loop.

target.component: PyNetworkFS TCP authentication and file-serving service
